key_insight: Support-constrained offline reinforcement learning improves estimated pediatric ECMO decision quality while staying closer to clinician behavior than standard Fitted Q-Iteration.
engineering_relevance: Empirical support constraints and clinician fallback offer a practical design pattern for limiting out-of-distribution actions in data-scarce clinical decision systems.
method: Use Support-Constrained Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI-SC) to restrict optimization to empirically supported state-action pairs.
Default to the clinician baseline in low-data regions.
Evaluate estimated value with Fitted Q-Evaluation (FQE), clinician-action disagreement, and a unified Balance Score.
evidence_signal: On 78 pediatric trajectories spanning over 6,000 clinical hours, FQI-SC improved Balance Score by 38% and reduced clinician-action disagreement by 71% versus FQI, while gaining 1.28 FQE units over imitation learning.
watch_item: Offline estimates and clinician agreement do not establish clinical safety or neurological benefit; prospective validation is needed before deployment.
paper_title: Support-Constrained Offline Policy Improvement for Pediatric ECMO from Limited Clinical Data
